headline: Figma MCP Goes Open Beta
subheadline: The Figma MCP server you've been building with just went open beta — plus Claude Code 2.5 dropped with multi-repo context that could change how you work across your white-label apps.

sections.label: Trending
sections.title: Figma MCP Server Open Beta — AI Agents Can Now Edit Canvas Directly
sections.description: As of March 24, Figma's MCP server is in open beta. AI agents can now directly edit the canvas while respecting your design system — components, variables, auto layout, the works. Nine community-built skills launched alongside it, including /figma-generate-design. This is exactly the territory you're building in. Worth studying what the community skills look like and how they compare to what you're doing for your white-label sport apps.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Claude Code 2.5: Multi-Repository Context Across 10 Codebases
sections.description: Anthropic dropped Claude Code 2.5 with native multi-repo awareness — it can now understand dependencies across up to 10 linked codebases simultaneously. If you're working across multiple white-label app repos with shared design system code, this could be a serious workflow upgrade for your Cursor + Claude Code setup.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Figma and Agentic Coding: Why MCP Integrations Matter
sections.description: A strategic angle on why Figma's MCP play matters for the broader product ecosystem. Notably: Figma plans to start enforcing AI credit limits, with options for additional credit subscriptions or pay-as-you-go. Worth knowing as you plan your MCP integration — there may be cost implications for how heavily agents interact with files.

sections.label: Watch
sections.title: AI + Design Systems in 2026: The Workflow I Actually Use
sections.description: A practitioner walkthrough of how someone uses AI to support a real, shipping design system — not theoretical, not hype. Could be interesting to compare notes against your own Figma MCP + Claude workflow and see if there are patterns you haven't considered for the white-label system.

sections.label: Concept of the day
sections.title: AI-Orchestrated Design Systems
sections.description: Design systems are shifting from static component libraries to AI-orchestrated ecosystems — where agents consume design tokens and components programmatically, not just humans. The interesting insight: organizations only started caring about proper standards once AI agents needed to read the data. Your obsession with clean tokens and variables? It's becoming the competitive moat.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Anthropic's March 2026 Roundup — What to Watch in April
sections.description: A clean summary of everything Anthropic shipped in March — from Opus 4.6 to Claude Code 2.5 to dozens of smaller updates. Useful as a single catch-up page so you know what's changed in your primary AI stack. Also previews what's coming in April, which could affect your MCP integration plans.

sections.label: Think about this
sections.title: You're building the thing the industry just validated
sections.description: Figma just launched open beta for the exact capability you've been building — MCP-powered AI agents that respect design systems. You're not catching up; you're already here. The question worth sitting with on today's walk: does this open beta make your internal tool more valuable (because it's customized to your white-label needs), or does it change what you should be building?
